Based on the provided context, banks reported the following impacts regarding the FDIC special assessment:

*   **Wells Fargo:** In Q1 2024, the bank recorded an additional $284 million ($0.06 per share) for the FDIC special assessment, reflecting recent updates from the FDIC including potential recoveries. This followed a $1.9 billion charge in the prior quarter (Q4 2023). In Q2 2024, Wells Fargo noted that it had not anticipated the $336 million of expense incurred in the first half of the year for this assessment, which was subsequently included in their updated full-year non-interest expense guidance.
*   **PNC Financial Services:** In Q1 2024, PNC reported a pretax, non-core, non-interest expense of $130 million ($103 million after tax) related to the increased FDIC special assessment. This amount was included in their total non-interest expense for the quarter.
*   **M&T Bank:** In Q1 2024, M&T excluded an additional FDIC special assessment from its adjusted diluted earnings per share calculation (which would have been $3.15 excluding it versus $3.02 GAAP). In Q2 2024, the bank reported $5 million related to the FDIC special assessment, compared to $29 million in the prior quarter (Q1 2024).
